analysis:
The supplied units are head-side text from docs/architecture/inference.md, lines 4495-5336. The change is documentation only; the patch excerpt shows a date bump, KV re-slice floor prose, a cluster-service health-file note, and wording changes to the cluster runtime facts and grant section. No executable code, configuration or wire format changes in the supplied evidence. I reviewed these against the threat model.

TB-002 and TB-007: the Qwen media and cluster ingress text describes request-owned lanes, host ledger charges, and prefix reuse disabled on the media path. These match the retained cache posture in T-041 (cacheSalt scoping and account-scoped prefix partitions). The text claims no relaxation of encryption, TTL or scope controls.

TB-011: the cluster grant text (lines 5254-5288) says a coordinator holds pair members without a grant to single-Mac requirements, and that grants bound the sessions a coordinator forms. It describes platform-owned policy and does not alter the App Attest authorization or receipt policy that the TB-011 and T-053 text defines. The clause that a declaration applies to the whole declared family on any Apple silicon pair is a documented design property. I cannot confirm from this excerpt that the platform enforces it, so the contract is unverified here, but it is not a regression.

The patch excerpt ends before the full runtime-facts change (about line 5234 onward). Wording changes in that section, including the platform-owned grant links, were not fully visible. The documentation overclaims nothing that I could see, such as qualification, runtime secrecy (T-056) or a production activation. A later pass could check the doc's cited behaviors (health-file PID guard, re-slice floors, grant scoping) against the corresponding source diffs in other batches. Those items are integration questions, not findings.
